tweets.text: RT @firesidealpha: Tom Mueller, SpaceX employee #1, says Elon Musk reversed his approach to engineering by demanding they find where rocket…

retweet.text:
Tom Mueller, SpaceX employee #1, says Elon Musk reversed his approach to engineering by demanding they find where rocket engines break and then push them harder

"It changed just working with Elon. At my previous company, it was like, you never blow up a rocket engine or fail a rocket engine. That's bad. This is bad karma. Never test, always have a lot of margin and make sure that you don't fail it."

"And Elon's whole thing was, well, let's find out where it breaks and then fix that and go and push it even more. So it's really a whole different way of thinking about it. Really refreshing, and you learn a lot."

"We had things that we thought would break that we couldn't break. Other things would break because the engineering is not always that deterministic. It's not always obvious. I'm amazed that this thing is still running."

quoted.text:
Joe Rogan reveals he watched a SpaceX launch with Elon Musk from the command center, and says the rockets explode because SpaceX pushes them to the limit on purpose

"It's not just that. It just shows a complete lack of understanding of what he's trying to accomplish. The whole reason why they're exploding is because you're pushing the tolerances. You're pushing it to the limit, and he expects them to explode. And then he finds out what the weak points are."

"I was actually in the command center watching one of the SpaceX launches. So we watched it from the ground. It takes off, and then we go upstairs, and I'm chilling with Elon. That was surreal. You want to talk surreal?"

"You're watching it on, like, a fucking dozen screens as it's flying over Australia, as it goes into the darkness of night on the dark side of the planet, and then it comes over on the other side into the brightness of the sun and then lands in the ocean. It was bananas."

"But they have all these sensors all over the thing, and so they're monitoring the hull, and the hull actually had a problem. It was leaking. So they're like, 'Well, might explode. Might explode.' You know, catastrophically entertaining. But they're doing it on purpose. That is how they find out how these things work."

tweets.text: RT @jamesenglish0: Dawn Ward was charged with racially aggravated assault after a man at Euston station accused her of a racist slur. Dawn…

retweet.text: Dawn Ward was charged with racially aggravated assault after a man at Euston station accused her of a racist slur. Dawn says she never said a word of it. Her lawyer didn't think she would go to jail, but warned her the worst case was jail. When she told her children what she was charged with, her youngest daughter Aston was 10. Aston asked if prison would let her out at least once a week to see them, or if she would come home every day. Dawn told her she wouldn't go to prison, because she didn't want her daughter worrying. That question made her want to fight more than ever. The case hung over her for two years, and a trial meant to last three days ran to nine. In the end all 12 jurors found her not guilty, and they waited outside the gates to tell her she should never have been in that courtroom.

quoted.text:
I used to think Trump Accounts were only for newborns because of the $1,000 government contribution. So I never bothered to set one up for my kids.

Out of my three children, two are already adults (over 18), so they aren’t eligible. But my youngest is still under 18, and yesterday I finally claimed and activated the account for him.

Turns out the account itself isn’t just for babies. Any child under 18 with a Social Security number can have one. The $1,000 seed money is only for kids born between 2025 and 2028, but older kids under 18 can still have the account.

Treasury automatically enrolled eligible children back in October 2026, but parents still need to claim and activate the account through the official app or website. Only then can you contribute money or receive outside contributions — including the SpaceX shares that Elon Musk and the company pledged to active accounts.

If you have a child under 18, it might be worth checking and claiming the account now. I almost missed it myself. https://t.co/y2uTwUBmn5
